$description: Antseed design tokens. Made by AstraOS for Antseed, v1, 12 Nov 2026. The source of every value in the kit: build.mjs turns it into tokens.css and the token tables in DESIGN.md. W3C Design Tokens format (draft): groups, $value, $type, $description, $extensions. Values are CSS-ready strings; {tier.name} is a reference to another token, and in tokens.css it becomes var(--that-token), so the themes stay live. Each token names its CSS variable in $extensions["kit.css"], the site's own name in $extensions["site-alias"] and the file and line it was read from on the live site (main ce969b4) in $extensions.source. Each tier's $description says how an agent may use it.

core.$description: Use freely. The few colours that carry the brand, the same in both themes.

green.$description: The action colour: the fill of every primary button, in both themes; green text, links and icons by day. One filled green button per group.

green-lip.$description: The darker lip at the foot of every green button (an inset shadow). At night the button keeps only this lip.

acid.$description: Light on dark: LEDs, cursors, the coin's glow at night, the dot-ants. Called lime in conversation. Never text on white (1.27:1).

ink.$description: The one ink: command lines, text inside product scenes, the darkest text. Kit merge (DECISIONS.md K09): the site also uses #090b0c (hero --ink, index.html:53), #001E12 (favicon mark), #000 (--title) and #1c1c1c (H1); the kit keeps #0a1a12 only.

night.$description: The dark page. Night paintings fade their top to exactly this colour.

night-surface.$description: The dark rail and dark surfaces; the Private by design section in both themes.

paper.$description: The light rail, the white of paper, button text.

page.$description: The light margins around the rail, under the dot matrix: a shade darker than the white inside.

theme.$description: Use for UI. The same names in both themes; tokens.css swaps them under [data-theme="dark"] and prefers-color-scheme.

page.$description: Margins around the rail, under the dot matrix.

rail.$description: The content column (the rail) and every surface on it.

text.$description: Text and the first half of every title (12.15:1 on white). Kit merge: titles are #30382c; the site's #000 product titles are folded in.

text-grey.$description: The grey second half of every two-tone title; feature icons. 3.11:1 on white, so large text only.

h1-second.$description: The H1's second line, as on the site: 4.48:1 on white at the H1's opacity .82, where the title grey would give 2.43:1. Section titles keep the title grey.

text-body.$description: Body copy under titles, captions' second line (6.02:1 on white).

text-small.$description: Small print, units, provider counts (4.91:1 on white).

green-text.$description: Green text, links and eyebrows (5.07:1 on white).

dot.$description: The margin dot matrix and every dotted outline.

tile.$description: The ghost button's fill and the model card's tile.

control-ring.$description: The warm hairline under tabs and round controls.

focus.$description: Focus ring, 2px solid. Kit merge (DECISIONS.md K09): the focus ring is the green; the hero's #789f00 is folded in.

button-fill.$description: Primary button fill: the same green in both themes.

button-text.$description: Primary button text. Kit merge: the nav's #fafafa is folded into #fff.

button-shadow.$description: Primary button depth: a soft drop, a pale lip and the green lip.

wash.$description: A landscape panel's own colour while its painting has not arrived yet.

logo-filter.$description: The black logo as it is.

page.$description: Margins around the rail at night.

text.$description: Text and titles at night (14.6:1 on the dark rail).

text-grey.$description: Every secondary text at night: the titles' grey half, body and small print share it (6.66:1 on the dark rail).

h1-second.$description: The H1's second line at night, as on the site (5.28:1 on the night page at opacity .82).

green-text.$description: Green text at night: the action green is 3.69:1 on #0f1312, this one 9.28:1 (8.46:1 on the dark rail). Not a third brand colour.

dot.$description: Dots at night, as visible on the dark rail as the light ones on white.

dot-off.$description: A dot bar's unlit dots at night.

tile.$description: Ghost button and card tile at night.

focus.$description: Focus ring at night: the night green text.

button-fill.$description: Buttons keep their green at night.

button-shadow.$description: At night no pale lip and no drop: only the green lip.

button-ghost-shadow.$description: Ghost button at night: a faint dark lip.

wash.$description: A landscape panel's own colour at night, before its painting arrives.

logo-filter.$description: At night the black logo is inverted to a neutral near-white (about #ededed): the site's way, for the logo on a coded page (class ak-logo). Anywhere else, use the near-white file (#eceee9) in files/logo/.

character-filter.$description: Every cut-out ant takes the night's light.

type.$description: Use for UI. Three families, weights 400 and 500 only, sentence case, tabular figures. Negative tracking only on the pixel display sizes and the lede.

sans.$description: Geist: body, ledes, buttons, labels. Google Fonts, OFL 1.1. Load: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Geist:wght@400;500&display=block, plus the arrows subset family=Geist:wght@400;500&text=%E2%86%92%E2%86%97 (Google's latin subset leaves out the arrows). Kit merge: Instrument Sans and Figtree, site leftovers, are folded into Geist.

mono.$description: Geist Mono: commands, prices, the terminal, technical captions. Google Fonts, OFL 1.1. Load: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Geist+Mono:wght@400;500&display=block

pixel.$description: Geist Pixel, variable on its ELSH axis (element shape, 0 to 100), self-hosted from GeistPixel-VariableFont_ELSH.ttf under the family name "Geist Pixel Var" (tokens.css declares it). Titles, eyebrows, figures. OFL 1.1. Google Fonts' plain family=Geist+Pixel request serves only the solid shape.

medium.$description: Buttons, names, links. The only other weight: nothing is loaded at 600 or 700, so a <b> would be a synthetic bold.

square.$description: Geist Pixel's Square instance: solid pixels. Not used on the page; the smaller a figure, the nearer this end it sits.

h1.$description: The H1's shape: square pixels with softened corners.

circle.$description: Round dots: eyebrows and key figures.

h1.$description: The display title: Geist Pixel ELSH 11, two tones (the text color, then the H1 grey #595959, #9ba49e at night), centered, opacity .82, no full stop. Tablet 8.4vw/1.04, phone 46/50.

section-title.$description: Section title: Geist Pixel ELSH 40, two halves, the second in text-grey, ending with a full stop. Phones 34/36, -1.4px.

eyebrow.$description: Eyebrow over a title: Geist Pixel ELSH 20 (16px × 1.125, line 1.5), green text, then a non-breaking space and ›. A link, usually to the docs.

figure.$description: A key figure under its label: Geist Pixel ELSH 20, tabular. Phones 26/26. Read live before use.

figure-large.$description: A large figure ($ANTS): Geist Pixel ELSH 20, tabular. 32/36 at 899px and below.

figure-name.$description: A point's name in pixel type ($ANTS points): ELSH 20.

lede.$description: The lede: Geist 400, the only text size with negative tracking. Phones 20/28.

sub.$description: The line under a title, in text-body. Phones 16/24.

body-strong.$description: A name at the start of a caption, in the text colour.

link.$description: A standalone link in green text: → to the docs and the page, ↗ to other sites.

card-name.$description: A model's name on its price card, two lines at most. Phones 14/18.

label.$description: A figure's label, over its value.

pill.$description: The announcement pill. The site sets it in Figtree 12/16; kit merge: Geist.

mono-price.$description: A price; its unit in text-small.

mono-saving.$description: A saving on a price card, in green text.

mono-caption.$description: A technical caption, lowercase, in green text.

space.$description: Use for UI. One 8px rhythm; the rail and its margins are clamps measured on Figma's 1504-wide frame.

grid.$description: The grid: the dot pitch, and every section's height snaps to a multiple of it so section tops land on the dots.

body-gutter.$description: The hero card floats 16px from the screen's edges.

gutter.$description: The dotted margin on each side of the rail (96 at 1504).

rail.$description: The rail's width; rounded down to a multiple of 16 where round() is supported (components.css .ak-rail), so its edges land on the dots.

section.$description: A section's top and bottom padding; 72px at 760px and below.

head-gap.$description: Between eyebrow, title and sub in a section head.

head-gap-tight.$description: The same in a product half or the prices head.

head-to-content.$description: From a section head to its panel or cards; 40px at 760px and below.

actions-row.$description: Row gap in a row of buttons.

actions-column.$description: Column gap in a row of buttons (12 in a product half).

duo-pad.$description: Padding of a product half's text.

duo-gap.$description: Between head, list and buttons in a product half.

feature-row.$description: A feature line's top and bottom padding.

icon-gap.$description: From a feature icon to its text.

icon.$description: A pixel icon: 24px, so each of its pixels is a whole 2px.

phone.$description: Breakpoint: phones at this width and below (one column, 72px sections, smaller titles). Media queries cannot read variables: write the number.

stack.$description: Breakpoint: product halves and points stack at this width and below.

tight.$description: Breakpoint: section grids tighten at this width and below.

radius.$description: Use for UI. Nested from the card (aside.com's scale, Elio's reference): what sits inside takes the next one down; where a box shares a corner with its parent, the outer radius less the inset, 2 at least. Buttons 10. Kit merge: the site's 12 and 14 leftovers are folded into this scale.

card.$description: Cards, card panels, model cards, the $ANTS and Private panels, the tooltip.

window.$description: A window in a card; the Gateway terminal; the Desktop window.

control.$description: Fields, buttons and rows inside a window.

min.$description: The floor where a box shares a corner with the one holding it.

button.$description: Every page button, primary and ghost.

dots.$description: Use for UI and effects. The dot is the ant: round, never square; dotted, never dashed; on the 8px grid. Effects made of dots (LED reveal, hover mosaic, dither) are drawn in code or the lab, never asked of an image model.

matrix.$description: The margin matrix (Figma's "Trame"): a 2px round dot every 8px, one on the page's centre line and one on its top edge. Set it as a background over the page colour.

outline.$description: One dot of a dotted outline: laid in strips 8px apart on each side that is switched on (components.css .ak-outline).

led-dot.$description: LED matrix (the painting's arrival and the hover mosaic): a dot's radius, times the 8px pitch.

hover-reach.$description: The hover mosaic's reach around the pointer. Mouse only, never on touch.

hover-half-life.$description: How fast the hover mosaic's trail fades.

sky-cell.$description: The hero sky's dither: 2px cells, ordered by an R2 sequence, not a Bayer matrix (which draws little crosses).

ant-radius.$description: A dot-ant: a round acid dot that walks the grid a cell at a time.

ant-ink.$description: The dot-ants' colour, with a glow rgba(200, 245, 60, .55) blurred 6px.

mosaic-pitch.$description: The Private by design mosaic's step; its dots 2.4px in radius.

motion.$description: Use for UI. Three curves do most of the work; four duration bands. Words first and still; arrive once; with reduced motion the finished still shows.

ease-arrive.$description: Arrivals: blocks rising into view, menus and rows coming in.

ease-slide.$description: State changes: tab lines and thumbs sliding, panels swapping.

ease-pop.$description: Small confirmations only: a check, a badge (strong overshoot).

ease-window.$description: A window popping in on its landscape (scale .9 to 1, slight overshoot).

dur-control.$description: Controls band, 350 to 450ms: tabs, toggles, menus.

dur-block.$description: Blocks band, 500 to 900ms: sections rising, the page's theme crossfade.

dur-painting.$description: Paintings band, 1.2 to 2.2s: the LED arrival of a painting, the night coming down.

dur-count.$description: A figure counting up to its live value once, exponential ease-out (1 - 2^-10k).

rise.$description: How far a block rises as it comes into view (panels 24px from scale .98).

glass.$description: Use for UI over paintings. By day the light window glass; at night every screen over a landscape is the smoked green glass. The Gateway terminal is smoked green in both themes.

day.$description: Day window glass over a landscape.

smoked.$description: Smoked green glass: the Gateway terminal in both themes, and every window over a landscape at night.

smoked-text.$description: Colours on smoked glass (the terminal): body text, commands, window chrome, the prompt, URLs, JSON, the caret, its dotted lines and its title bar. Tuned for 4.5:1 over a bright sky.

smoked-thin.$description: Thinner smoked glass (Private by design's windows, both themes): more painting shows; the frost dims what is under it so light text still reads.

popover.$description: A menu or popover by day.

popover-night.$description: A menu or popover at night: the same green, denser.

pill.$description: The announcement pill by day, as on the live hero (Whimsical 2).

pill-acid.$description: The acid pill of the hero's other versions, ink text. By day only.

pill-night.$description: At night the pill is neutral glass, so the hero's only green is its button.

button.$description: Use for UI. One filled green button per group, then ghosts. Same radius for both.

shadow-light.$description: Primary by day: a soft drop, a pale lip, the green lip.

shadow-dark.$description: Primary at night: only the green lip.

illustration.$description: Drawings and code effects only, never UI.

night-character.$description: Every cut-out ant at night: a little darker, cooler, less saturated, as the painting behind it. Also the night reference for assets made off the site (DECISIONS.md K20).

$extensions.site-alias: filter on the mascot at night

seed-night-glow.$value: drop-shadow(0 0 6px rgba(255, 200, 100, .85)) drop-shadow(0 0 22px rgba(255, 150, 50, .62)) drop-shadow(0 0 56px rgba(255, 128, 32, .4))
seed-night-glow.$description: A seed glowing amber at night.

coin-night-glow.$description: The $ANTS coin at night: an acid glow.

fireflies.$description: The hero's night fireflies, drawn in code (never painted).

local.$description: Never outside their scene. Kept so nobody mistakes them for brand colours.

network.$description: The network board only (in progress, left out of the kit's page): your links in electric blue, others' links faint, cream bases for people, green for providers.

window-lights.$description: macOS traffic lights on the terminal and app windows.

desktop-app.$description: Antseed Desktop's own app colours, drawn over its captures. The app's navy night differs from the site's green-black on purpose (DECISIONS.md K19).
